must_not_miss.text: The auditors' report is DUAL-DATED: "March 7, 2022, except as to Note 27, which is as of April 22, 2022."
must_not_miss.why: A dual date is the auditor formally limiting how far forward their responsibility runs. It is one line, in a signature block, on the last page of the audit report — and it is the strongest single signal in the document that something went wrong after publication.

must_not_miss.text: The Board of Governors signature block on the balance sheet has TWO BLANK 'Governor' lines.
must_not_miss.why: The statements are presented "On behalf of the Board of Governors" over two unsigned lines. Extractors reliably drop signature blocks entirely.

must_not_miss.text: Note 27 exists at all — a restatement OF the already-restated statements, made after issuance for errors discovered post-publication.
must_not_miss.why: Second-to-last note in a 70-page document. This is the archetypal buried item: the most damaging disclosure, placed last.

must_not_miss.text: Uncertified class action claims relating to a DATA BREACH, plus claims from employees.
must_not_miss.why: A data breach is disclosed nowhere else in the report — not in the MD&A, not in the risk note. It appears once, in a subclause of the contingencies note.

must_not_miss.text: Firm Capital Corporation lent at the higher of 8.50% or TD prime + 6.05%; the province's replacement facility charged 1.11%.
must_not_miss.why: Neither rate is remarkable alone; the pair is the story. Requires joining two notes at opposite ends of the document, which is exactly what section-chunked extraction does badly.

must_not_miss.text: A new $590 thousand administrative fee charged against endowment investment income (2020 – nil), alongside the distribution policy cut from 3.5% to 2.0%.
must_not_miss.why: LU began charging the endowment a fee it had never charged, in the year it went insolvent. One sentence, end of a dense policy paragraph.

must_not_miss.text: LU is principal employer of a Pension Plan that also covers the Federated Universities, SNOLAB, CEMI and MIRARCO. Huntington employees ceased accruing 30 June 2021; University of Sudbury and Thorneloe employees became suspended members after 31 December 2021.
must_not_miss.why: The blast radius of the pension problem extends to four other institutions. Buried in the fifth subclause of the contingencies note.

must_not_miss.text: LU participates in a reciprocal insurance exchange sharing property and liability risk with forty other Canadian universities.
must_not_miss.why: A contingent, shared liability with 40 institutions. A single sentence, no dollar figure attached.

must_not_miss.text: The TD Canada Trust short-term loan financed the Student Recreation Centre; the CCAA filing was an event of default that made it due on demand.
must_not_miss.why: Names both the lender and what the money built. Short note, sandwiched between two longer ones.

must_not_miss.text: The government support package is CONDITIONAL on renewal of the Board of Governors and completion of a long-term strategic plan; first phase of Board renewal began 16 Dec 2021.
must_not_miss.why: The province made governance change a condition of the money. Last paragraph of the subsequent-events note.

Y.summary: This is the restated annual financial report for Laurentian University of Sudbury for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2021, audited by KPMG LLP with a going-concern emphasis paragraph. The report covers a landmark year in which Laurentian filed for CCAA protection on February 1, 2021, triggering a $66.7 million deficiency of revenues over expenses (including $78.9 million in one-time restructuring costs) against total revenue of $193.4 million. Total liabilities ballooned to $396.5 million, driven by $186.8 million reclassified to liabilities subject to compromise, while long-term debt collapsed to nil as $89.9 million in debt was stayed and reclassified. The University received a DIP loan from Firm Capital Corporation (later refinanced by the Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities at $35 million), terminated its federated university relationships with Thorneloe, University of Sudbury, and Huntington University, and closed 66 academic programs. The financial statements were originally issued March 7, 2022 and subsequently amended (Note 27) as of April 22, 2022, and also incorporate restatements of the FY2020 comparative figures disclosed in Note 25; the auditor's report carries two emphasis-of-matter paragraphs — going concern and restatement — without a modified opinion.

The University had access to a Royal Bank unsecured line of credit of $5.0 million and a Desjardins unsecured line of credit of $26.0 million in 2020; both lines were no longer available at April 30, 2021; at April 30, 2020 the Desjardins line had $14.4 million drawn.

MIRARCO (Mining Innovation Rehabilitation and Applied Research Corporation) is a wholly controlled subsidiary of Laurentian; SNOlab is a not-for-profit partnership in which Laurentian recognizes its proportionate 20% share of revenues and expenses.

NOSM occupied University campus buildings under a nominal lease; the University had $393 thousand receivable from NOSM and stayed payables of $1.4 million to NOSM at April 30, 2021. Ontario government introduced proposed legislation on April 15, 2021 to establish NOSM as an independent degree-granting institution.

CEMI (Centre for Excellence in Mining and Innovation) was created on April 23, 2007 with a $10 million contribution from Laurentian funded by the Provincial Government; the University has no claim to CEMI's assets nor liability for its obligations.
The University guaranteed a loan of $8.5 million for the Laurentian University Students' General Association for construction of a student centre.

The FY2021 financial statements were restated after original issuance (Note 27): Other fees and income reduced by $2.138 million, salaries reduced by $0.141 million, operating and research expenses reduced by $1.075 million, and restructuring costs reduced by $0.233 million; employee future benefit remeasurements increased by $0.689 million. The deficiency of revenue over expenses changed from $65.982 million to $66.671 million.
The government support package conditions include renewal of the Board of Governors and completion of a long-term strategic plan; the first phase of Board renewal commenced December 16, 2021.
The University operated a $63 million campus modernization program initiated in 2014, financed primarily by debt of $91.3 million as of February 1, 2021.

Provincial performance-based funding (SMA3) for 2020-21 and 2021-22 was decoupled from performance metrics due to COVID-19; Laurentian would have obtained its full $16.2 million performance grant allocation in 2020-21 if it had been activated.
There are uncertified class action claims against the University related to a data breach, as well as claims from employees; these are subject to measurement uncertainty.

The TD Canada Trust short-term loan of $1.324 million (used to finance the Student Recreation Centre, floating rate of 1.42%) was classified to liabilities subject to compromise; the CCAA filing on February 1, 2021 was an event of default.

Endowment net assets grew to $61.5 million at April 30, 2021 from $54.3 million at April 30, 2020, driven by $8.2 million in investment income (compared to a $0.6 million decline the prior year); the endowment distribution policy was reduced to 2.0% of the 12-month fair value (from 3.5% prior year).

The University's Note 25 comparative restatements corrected multiple prior-period errors including: failure to record the Pension Benefit Guarantee Fund accrual (PBGF — understating liabilities by $702 thousand), understatement of accrued vacation pay by $747 thousand, errors in endowment allocation over 17 years understating endowment by $1.454 million, and misclassification of $1.119 million of endowment investments as short-term cash.
Excluding the impact of CCAA restructuring costs and prior-period adjustments, management calculates an adjusted excess of revenue over expenses of $12.2 million for fiscal 2021.

Z.summary: This is the audited annual financial report of Laurentian University of Sudbury for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2021, covering the period in which Laurentian filed for and operated under CCAA insolvency protection. The University recorded a deficiency of revenue over expenses of $66.7 million on total revenue of $193.4 million and total expenses of $260.1 million, including $78.9 million of one-time CCAA restructuring costs. Total liabilities reached $396.5 million against total assets of $381.1 million, leaving a net asset deficiency of $15.4 million. KPMG LLP issued an unqualified audit opinion with a material uncertainty going concern paragraph and two emphasis-of-matter paragraphs noting a restatement of the 2021 statements (Note 27, dated April 22, 2022) and a restatement of 2020 comparative information (Note 25); the financial statements themselves were twice restated after original issuance. Key restructuring events include the February 1, 2021 CCAA filing, appointment of Ernst & Young Inc. as monitor, a super-priority DIP loan from Firm Capital Corporation later refinanced by the Ontario government, closure of 39 English and 27 French programs, termination of the federated university relationships with Thorneloe, University of Sudbury and Huntington, and significant amendments to pension and benefit plans.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury filed for CCAA protection and obtained an Initial Order from the Chief Justice of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) on February 1, 2021.
key_facts.quote: On February 1, 2021, Laurentian obtained an Order from the Chief Justice of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) (the 'CCAA Court').

key_facts.fact: Ernst & Young Inc. was appointed as Monitor of Laurentian pursuant to an Order of the CCAA Court on February 1, 2021.
The CCAA Court approved a super-priority, non-revolving DIP credit facility of up to $25 million on February 10, 2021, provided by Firm Capital Corporation as DIP lender.
The DIP facility was increased to $35 million on May 19, 2021, with the initial draw of $10 million received on February 16, 2021 and a second draw of $15 million on March 26, 2021.

The DIP Loan bore interest at the higher of 8.50% or TD Canada Trust Posted Bank Prime Interest Rate plus 6.05%; the University paid $591 in debt issuance costs and recognized $583 in interest expense.

On December 16, 2021, the Ontario Government announced a support package through the Ministry of Colleges and Universities: $35 million to refinance the DIP Loan, up to $6 million in COVID-19 grant funding, and up to $22 million in enrolment corridor and performance protection.
On January 27, 2022, the Court authorized the Replacement DIP Facility from MCU not exceeding $35 million; funds were advanced on January 28, 2022 at an interest rate of 1.11%.
The stay of CCAA proceedings was extended multiple times and was most recently extended to May 31, 2022.
Laurentian approved the closure of 39 English-language programs and 27 French-language programs as part of the CCAA restructuring.

Laurentian terminated its federated relationships with Thorneloe University, University of Sudbury and Huntington University through a court-approved statutory mechanism; payments to these federated universities amounted to $7.7 million in 2020-21.

Total CCAA restructuring costs recognized in 2020-21 were $78.9 million, comprising: termination of interest rate swaps $24.7 million; workforce adjustments and termination costs $44.7 million (plus $0.7 million for third-party Retirees' Health Benefit Plan); legal, monitor, and consulting costs of $8.8 million.

The University recognized a $24.7 million loss on termination of seven interest rate swap agreements on February 1, 2021, as CCAA filing constituted an event of default triggering termination by bank counterparties.
Total revenue for fiscal 2020-21 was $193.4 million, a decrease of $4.2 million (2.1%) from $197.6 million in the prior year.

Total expenses for fiscal 2020-21 were $260.1 million, including restructuring costs of $78.9 million; excluding restructuring, expenses were $181.2 million, down $19.7 million (9.8%) from the prior year.
Deficiency of revenues over expenses for fiscal 2020-21 was $66.7 million, compared to a deficiency of $3.4 million in the prior year.

Operating grants and contracts revenue was $79.3 million (40.6% of total revenue), down $6.9 million from the prior year; this included $54.3 million in core operating and performance grants, $8.3 million in Bilingualism Grant, and $6.2 million in Northern Grant.

Tuition and ancillary fees revenue increased from $53.2 million in 2019-20 to $58.3 million in 2020-21, driven by higher online enrolment; international tuition fees were $13.6 million, an 11.5% increase.

Research grants and contracts recognized were $22.4 million in 2020-21, a decrease of $1.7 million (7.0%) from $24.2 million in the prior year; unspent research funding as deferred contributions was $18.6 million at April 30, 2021.
Salaries and benefits expense was $128.4 million in 2020-21, $6.4 million lower than the prior year.
Total assets at April 30, 2021 were $381.1 million; total liabilities were $396.5 million; net assets were a deficiency of $15.4 million.
Cash and short-term investments at April 30, 2021 were $37.0 million, up from $3.4 million at April 30, 2020, largely due to the $25 million DIP financing.
Long-term investments (endowment funds) at April 30, 2021 were $62.2 million, up $8.2 million from the prior year.
Net investment in capital assets was $263.4 million at April 30, 2021 compared to $272.5 million in 2020; capital additions were $1.4 million.

Liabilities subject to compromise at April 30, 2021 totalled $186.8 million, consisting of: accounts payable $11.3 million, employee future benefits liabilities $13,973 (reclassified from balance sheet), employee restructuring and termination costs $59.6 million, short-term loan $1.3 million, long-term debt $89.9 million, and interest rate swap termination obligation $24.7 million.

Total claims asserted by creditors pursuant to CCAA claims procedures were $360.3 million, versus $186.8 million recognized as liabilities subject to compromise; the difference is not yet recognized as the University is still assessing claims.

Long-term debt at April 30, 2021 was classified as $0 in long-term (all $89.9 million reclassified to liabilities subject to compromise); prior year long-term debt was $89.0 million. The debt consisted of unsecured loans with Bank of Montreal, Royal Bank of Canada, and TD Canada Trust at rates ranging from 3.90% to 5.39%, maturing between 2023 and 2043.
The University ceased accruing interest on long-term debt as of February 1, 2021 due to the CCAA event of default.
The University had a Royal Bank unsecured line of credit of $5 million and a Desjardins unsecured line of credit of $26 million in 2020; both were no longer available at April 30, 2021.

The Retirees' Health Benefit Plan (RHBP) and Supplementary Pension Plan (SuRP) were both terminated on April 30, 2021; the RHBP had obligations of $10.8 million and the SuRP had obligations of $3.2 million, both reclassified to liabilities subject to compromise.

The Pension Plan was amended effective April 2021 and renamed the Retirement Plan of Laurentian University of Sudbury effective July 1, 2021; amendments included career average earnings formula (replacing best average earnings), elimination of guaranteed post-retirement indexation, and modification of early retirement benefits. A new actuarial valuation as of July 1, 2021 showed improvement; no special pension payments required until the next valuation on July 1, 2024.

Pension Plan accrued benefit obligation at April 30, 2021 was $452.2 million; fair value of plan assets was $461.7 million, yielding a surplus of $9.5 million; however, the University recorded a $9.5 million allowance for benefit reinstatement, resulting in no net pension asset on the balance sheet.
The University's combined accumulated unrestricted fund deficit and employee benefit liabilities had grown to $42.2 million at the end of April 2020 prior to the CCAA filing.
Enrolment (FTE) for 2020-21 was 7,090, up from 6,834 the prior year; fall 2020 headcount was 9,323, a 4.2% increase, driven primarily by online enrolment growth of 26% (headcount).
Subsequent to fiscal year end, total enrolment (headcount) fell 14% for fall 2021; preliminary estimates for fall 2022 showed another significant decline due to CCAA uncertainty.
The CCAA restructuring reduced annual operating expenses by approximately $40 million (25%) per year.

On April 5, 2021, the University entered into a term sheet with LUSU; on April 7, 2021, the University and LUFA signed a term sheet including a new collective agreement, faculty complement reduction, and pension and benefits amendments.
The deferred maintenance backlog was estimated at $135 million; only $1.4 million was invested in capital projects in 2020-21, funded by MCU Facility Renewal Program grants.
The University had guaranteed a loan for the Laurentian University Students' General Association for $8.5 million for construction of a student centre; no event of default occurred in 2020-21.
NOSM occupied and leased buildings on the University's campus for a nominal amount; at April 30, 2021, the University had $393 receivable from NOSM and $1,412 in stayed payables to NOSM.
Ontario government introduced proposed legislation to establish NOSM as an independent degree-granting institution on April 15, 2021.

KPMG LLP issued an unqualified audit opinion with a material uncertainty going concern paragraph (Note 2) and two emphasis-of-matter paragraphs: one noting the restatement of the originally issued 2021 financial statements (Note 27, dated April 22, 2022) and one noting restatement and correction of 2020 comparative information (Note 25).
KPMG's original audit report was dated March 7, 2022; a subsequent Note 27 restatement amendment was dated April 22, 2022.

The 2021 financial statements were restated after original issuance (Note 27) to correct errors in revenue, expenses and remeasurement gains: Other fees and income decreased by $2.138 million; Salaries reduced by $141 thousand, Operating and research by $1.075 million, Restructuring costs by $233 thousand; Employee future benefits remeasurements increased by $689 thousand. Net effect on deficiency: reduced deficiency by $689 thousand.

The 2020 comparative financial statements were restated in Note 25 for multiple prior period errors including: PBGF accrual omission ($702 thousand); accrued vacation pay understatement ($747 thousand); endowment allocation errors ($1.454 million understatement); misclassification of $1.119 million of short-term investments; and Retiree Health Benefit Plan funded plan asset errors ($1.769 million). Prior year net assets were restated from $36.7 million to $34.8 million.

Deferred contributions at April 30, 2021 totalled $36.4 million (research grants $18.6 million, other grants and trust $14.7 million, scholarships $3.1 million); only $4.4 million was supported by cash in separate bank accounts, while $32.0 million was not backed by segregated cash.
Endowment net assets at April 30, 2021 were $61.5 million, up from $54.3 million; cumulative endowment contributions were $50.0 million and cumulative reinvested income was $11.5 million.
The endowment distribution policy was set at 2.0% of the last 12 months fair value for fiscal 2021, down from 3.5% the prior year.

MIRARCO is a wholly controlled entity consolidated by the University; SNOLab is a not-for-profit partnership with four other universities in which the University recognizes its proportionate 20% share.
Capital assets at cost were $450.4 million with accumulated amortization of $187.0 million, yielding net book value of $263.4 million; buildings comprised the largest component at $243.0 million net.
The University is involved in uncertified class action claims related to a data breach and claims from employees whose outcomes are not presently determinable.
The University's $63 million campus modernization program (initiated in 2014) was financed primarily by debt of $91.3 million as of February 1, 2021, all of which was stayed under CCAA.

The University's prior accumulated unrestricted deficit and employee benefit liabilities had driven recurring operating deficits over several years; factors included declining domestic enrolment (2015-16 to 2019-20) and a provincial 10% domestic tuition reduction in 2019-20 followed by a freeze in 2020-21.

The McEwen School of Architecture became the 12th accredited architectural school in Canada, with the professional Master of Architecture program receiving Initial Accreditation from CACB/CCCA for a term commencing July 1, 2021.

The University recognized $22.4 million in research grants and contracts in 2020-21, with researchers including Dr. Stefan Siemann (Canadian Foundation for Innovation grant), Dr. Dave Pearson (Natural Resources Canada grant with First Nations partners), and Dr. Joey-Lynn Wabie (Heritage Canada grant).
The government support conditions include renewal of the Board of Governors and completion of a long-term strategic plan; the first phase of Board renewal commenced December 16, 2021.

Effective June 30, 2021, all Huntington University active employees ceased accruing entitlement in the Pension Plan; University of Sudbury and Thorneloe University employees employed after December 31, 2021 will become suspended members.
